title: Clear a cable-tie offcut from a Jetson controller fan
instruction: Restore the controller cooling fan and put the removed debris in the parts tray.
context: Jetson computers run robot perception and control. A loose cable-tie offcut trapped in a small cooling fan interrupts cooling during hardware service. This task requires extracting the real obstruction through a wire guard and checking sustained forward rotation while leaving the mounted controller intact.
setup: Two YAM parallel-gripper arms at the standard station table (1.10 x 1.30 m wood top, z=0.7475 m). A Jetson Nano 2GB developer kit has a 100 x 79 x 1.57 mm FR4 carrier, source connector housings and aluminium heatsink; its board datum is (0.30,-0.08,0.7595) m. It is screwed to four 6 mm diameter x 9 mm nylon standoffs on a 115 x 95 x 3 mm insulating plate fixed to the bench. A Delta AFB0405MA-AFGE-compatible 5 V fan has a 40 x 40 x 10 mm plastic frame and independent plastic impeller, mounted over the heatsink with base at (0.30,-0.0777,0.7877712) m. Four 0.9 mm diameter insulated leads connect it to J7. A nickel-chromed steel Orion G40-2 wire guard (1.6 mm wire,32 mm square mounting pattern) is screwed on top. One unattached natural PA66 Panduit SG100M-C offcut is 80.2 x 3.0 x 1.0 mm, mass 0.274 g; it leans through an outer guard gap and is caught between the impeller and frame. Its exposed end is about 41 mm above the fan base after settling, as shown in the setup image. A 5 V 3 A USB-C supply outside the work area feeds a fixed 60 x 26 x 12 mm plastic inline rocker at (0.17,-0.19,0.7475) m through a 3.8 mm insulated cable; the rocker starts ON. A fixed blue plastic tray 106 x 106 x 20 mm is centred at (0.30,-0.25,0.7475) m, empty. Free steel/polymer long-nose pliers 235 x 69 x 24 mm,180 g, and a PH1 screwdriver 147 x 27 x 26 mm,100 g, lie at source origins (0.42,0.11,0.7475) m and (0.42,0.19,0.7475) m. All dimensions are physical, with no object randomization. CAD, asset IDs, source hashes and the deterministic settling layout are in the folder.
scoring: Scored at the end. 0 if a mounted board, fan frame or guard is displaced more than 2 mm or rotated more than 3 degrees, or a finger or tool enters the powered/coasting blade region during the trial. Coasting lasts after isolation until rotor speed first falls to at most 1 rad/s; subsequent deliberate manual rotation is allowed. The rotor region is radius 18.5 mm and z=3.0..10.4 mm relative to the fan base; finger checks use reconstructed finger boxes/surface samples. Tool checks conservatively use oriented bounds of the actual collision meshes against the enclosing 37 x 37 x 7.4 mm blade box. Otherwise 0 until the complete offcut centreline is more than 29 mm from the fan centre at z=5.2 mm. Clearance alone earns 0.3. Containment earns 0.6 only when every offcut corner lies within the tray interior |x|,|y|<49 mm and z=2..20.5 mm, its linear speed is below 20 mm/s, and fingers and service-tool bounds are at least 20 mm from it. Full score 1.0 additionally requires the fan powered and rotating forward above 4000 RPM continuously for 10 seconds with the offcut clear. Reverse motion does not count. Rotation can be checked with a handheld tachometer; dimensions and release with a ruler/video. In physical trials, inspect before and after: any new visible crack, broken blade, detached wire or missing fastener scores 0 at every tier. The rigid simulation does not model these failures: its integrity checks are only the stated pose and intrusion proxies, and a nonzero simulator score does not certify absence of real damage. All other outcomes receive the highest satisfied tier.
run_limit: 600 control steps (30 seconds at 20 Hz); physics runs at 2400 Hz.
reset_notes: De-energize the controller, wait for the rotor to stop, clear the tray, and restore the same free offcut and tool layout. Keep board, fan, guard and service plate fastenings installed. Simulation reset restores the authored layout then settles for 0.5 seconds; no pieces are attached or released by task state.
fidelity: Manufacturer Jetson/Delta/Orion geometry at original scale. Blade/offcut contact is simulated; no release rules. Rigid PA66 omits bending/fracture; mounting fasteners fixed. Rotor mass/torque and coast drag estimated; no electrical/thermal failure model. Static wiring and simplified rocker. Finger safety uses symmetric kinematic bounds; tools use collision-mesh bounds. Small electronics are visual and tool joints are fused.
